mindsetSubtitle.message: Engineered around ocular physiology and flow-state reading comprehension.

pillar1Desc.message: Single-word flashers don't help with the mental-model and the ability to follow syntax of sentences.  ParaFlow Reader projects a dimmed Ghost Line above the active word and a Lookahead Horizon below it, preserving syntactic structure in working memory across every fixation.  Giving your eyes the opportunity to escape the confined space by which older readers did not allow.

pillar2Desc.message: Mechanical speed readers tick at flat millisecond intervals. Human comprehension does not. ParaFlow scales multiple-factors with display duration dynamically matching cognitive processing pauses.  But it's not a locked box, take a peek, adjust settings to your liking.

pillar3Desc.message: What's your style? We don't want to decide for. Is it the ORP? The Optical Recognition Point sits between 30% and 40% of word length. -- Or is it gentle themes or getting into a Flow State that get's your mind going. ParaFlow Reader positions characters but you decide everything else.

pillar4Desc.message: The extension runs on your device and stores any used required data strictly in browser memory so it forgets it when you leave the page.  Content is parsed from the larger text-body on the page and is processed through a sandbox (completely seperated from current page).

practiceKicker.description: Kicker text for How to Improve Reading Comprehension

practiceSubtitle.message: Transitioning from phonological vocalization or voiced-reading to direct orthographic pattern recognition follows measurable stages. Find your pace with the following benchmarks:

phase1Desc.message: Lock foveal focus to the vertical reticle tick-marker. Keep three-word chunks active with lookahead enabled. Train the extraocular muscles to hold position rather than jumping laterally.

phase2Desc.message: Above 350 WPM, vocal cords and the inner speech loop cannot keep pace. The visual cortex takes over direct lexical access. Punctuation weighting prevents working memory overload.

phase3Desc.message: Reduce chunk size to two words. Rely on the lookahead line to pre-parse clauses before they reach center focus. The Ghost Line catches syntactically complex subordinate clauses.

phase4Desc.message: Deploy single-word spotlighting with maximum punctuation weighting. This mode extracts arguments, variable names, and factual data points from dense technical documentation.

taxSubtitle.message: Formal definitions from cognitive psychology and ocular motor research.

defParafoveal.message: The retinal zone spanning 2° to 5° around the foveal center. Acuity is lower than foveal vision, but the visual cortex extracts word length, initial consonants, and space boundaries to program the amplitude of upcoming saccades.

defOrp.message: The ocular fixation point within a word that minimizes letter recognition latency. For Latin scripts, this point sits between 30% and 40% of the total word length from the initial character.

defGhostLine.message: A dimmed rendering of the preceding text line displayed directly above active reading coordinates. It provides working memory with an immediate syntactic anchor when parsing multi-clause sentences.

defLookahead.message: Configurable upcoming text lines displayed below the active word chunk. It provides parafoveal preview data so the brain preprocesses downstream syntactic units before fixating upon them.

termCadence.description: Taxonomy term for punctuation cadence multiplier

defCadence.message: A dynamic scaling algorithm that extends tick duration at punctuation boundaries: 1.35x for commas and semicolons, 1.8x for sentence terminators, and 2.2x for paragraph breaks.

defSaccade.message: An involuntary backwards eye jump triggered when sentence comprehension fails. In conventional reading, regressions account for 15% to 25% of total ocular movements.
